source.title: Stanford CS224N Spring 2024 Lecture 1: Intro and Word Vectors

annotation_note: Claims and gold labels are manually written paraphrases of the linked public lecture at the listed time ranges. The raw auto-captions are downloaded for each run and are not committed. This small audit is not a general semantic-accuracy benchmark.

cases.text: The lecture describes a one-hot code as assigning a separate coordinate to each vocabulary item.
A large vocabulary can lead to long one-hot vectors.
The lecture says one-hot word codes do not inherently represent semantic meaning or similarity.
The lecture says distinct one-hot codes make hotel and motel appear semantically similar.
A larger vocabulary may increase the storage cost of one-hot word codes.
The lecture fixes every learned word vector at exactly 300 dimensions.
The lecture describes softmax as converting scores into a probability distribution over context words.
The probability calculation considers each possible context word before normalization.
After softmax, the outputs remain unnormalized real-valued logits.
Normalizing over a large set of possible context words may increase computation.
The lecture guarantees that its softmax probabilities are perfectly calibrated.
